source.title: Understanding the role of individual units in a deep neural network
source.authors: David Bau; Jun-Yan Zhu; Hendrik Strobelt; Àgata Lapedriza; Bo-Lei Zhou; A. Torralba

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies interpretable and causally important units in visual CNNs and GANs, but does not test any of the listed claim versions: it does not audit language-model neuron poles, compare the specified shares across models or tools, assess the cited Inception examples, or build attribution graphs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports visual-unit concept matches and unit interventions. These results concern the claim's broad subject, but their measurements and models do not test the specific versions listed. Values such as IoU thresholds are used to identify units, not results about the listed claims.
record.test_reason: Network dissection of a VGG-16 scene classifier and Progressive GANs. It matches units to segmented concepts and intervenes on them. It reports no share of units with one or two jobs and no language-model audit. It makes no cross-architecture or tool comparison of interpretable shares in the main text, no InceptionV1 pose analysis, no attribution graphs, and no simulation-based scoring. None of its results bear on whether a listed version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that systematic analysis and manipulation of individual units reveal the structure of knowledge learned by classifiers and generators. They also note that the method relies on disentangled interpretable units emerging during training.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses network dissection: it matches visual-unit activations to image segmentations and intervenes on visual CNN and GAN units. It does not use language-model neuron explanations or score explanations on held-out text.
record.method_sensitivity: For GAN door-unit activation, the outcome depends on feature-map location and scene context.

fits_no_version.finding: A unit labelled by IoU predicts its concept on out-of-domain data only imperfectly. Unit 150 reaches 85.6% balanced accuracy for airplanes on ImageNet. The GAN window unit reaches 78.2%, and large windows are often generated without it activating.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In vision CNNs/GANs, concept labels assigned to single units by segmentation IoU predict the concept's presence well above chance but incompletely.

fits_no_version.finding: Units important to many classes are more interpretable by IoU than units important to one class or none (Fig. 2e).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a scene-classifier CNN, unit interpretability correlates with the number of classes the unit is important to.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating or forcing small sets of concept-matched units causally changes class accuracy or generated objects, in a context-dependent way.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept-matched units in visual classifiers and GANs have concept-specific causal roles.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
record.problems: The paper reports imperfect reference segmentation performance (mean IoU 23.4% on objects, 28.8% on parts, and 54.2% on materials). It also reports counterexamples for the window unit: images with large windows can be generated without that unit activating. Some uncertainty intervals are shown in figures but their numeric endpoints are not given in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted secondary measurements not needed to record the direct unit-concept and unit-intervention findings, including all-class accuracy changes accompanying some ski-resort ablations, detailed door-pixel location results in Figure 4d, and unit changes in the adversarial-attack application in Figure 5. These do not test a listed claim version.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B or any language-model neuron-pole audit.
No language models, no dense versus MoE comparison, no scale comparison.
No InceptionV1 cat/car neuron, pose, or recursive-generalization analysis.
No interpretable-unit share across tools or architectures in the main text. AlexNet/ResNet comparisons are deferred to SI, which was not supplied. No InceptionV1-sized estimates.
No attribution graphs or replacement-model comparison.
No test of activating-example explanations against held-out firing. Labels come from segmentation IoU, not from inspecting examples.
No simulation-based scoring of explanations on text.

record.verdict_notes: Vision-only network dissection study, outside the claim's versions. The interpretable-concept counts are per concept, or per unit only above an IoU > 4% cut, and are not shares of units with one job. They cannot be read as V4 evidence without the SI. The paper's own reference segmenter is weak (object mIoU 23.4%), which bounds any interpretability count.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or estimate of the share of neuron poles with one or two jobs or that are not understood.
No cross-language-model, dense-versus-MoE, or trillion-parameter comparison.
No analysis of InceptionV1 cat-and-car units, pose, or recursive generalization.

The paper analyzes visual models, but does not compare interpretability shares across tools or architectures, explain messy late-layer units by architecture or regularization, or report the essay's InceptionV1-sized estimates.
No attribution graphs, large language model, or comparison with a trained replacement model and its reconstruction error.
No test of explanations against held-out neuron-activating examples or where neurons fire.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Matched units in conv5_3 to segmented visual concepts using network dissection; reported categories with IoU above 4%.
rows.measure: Number of distinct concepts matched by units, grouped by concept type
rows.value: 51 object classes, 22 parts, 12 materials, and 8 colors
rows.locator: Results, Emergence of Object Detectors in a Scene Classifier; Figure 1d
rows.note: Counts are concept categories matched, not the fraction of units with a single job.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated unit 150 as an airplane classifier on ImageNet using a peak-activation threshold.
rows.measure: Balanced accuracy distinguishing airplane classes from other object classes
rows.locator: Results, Emergence of Object Detectors in a Scene Classifier; Figure 1f
rows.note: This evaluates one visual unit's object-detection performance, not a language-model neuron explanation.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Set the four most important conv5_3 units for ski resort classification to zero.
rows.locator: Results, Role of Units in a Scene Classifier; Figure 2a-b
rows.note: The paper reports this as the effect of removing those units.
rows.check: The state is set against no version. The 81.4% to 64.0% drop is the study's own reported ablation effect, so 'partial' has no reference. It is better read as observed for the study's claim.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Set the 20 most important conv5_3 units for ski resort classification to zero.
rows.locator: Results, Role of Units in a Scene Classifier; Figure 2b
rows.note: The paper describes this as near chance; chance is 50%.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Removed the 492 least-important conv5_3 units, leaving the 20 most important units intact.
rows.locator: Results, Role of Units in a Scene Classifier; Figure 2b
rows.note: The study says this removal reduced ski resort accuracy by 3.7%.
rows.check: Control row. The 3.7% drop is the expected small effect, so 'partial' is misleading. It is linked to no version.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Removed each class's 20 most important conv5_3 units, separately for the 365 scene classes.
rows.locator: Results, Role of Units in a Scene Classifier; Figure 2d
rows.note: The paper describes the mean as near chance.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Removed each class's 492 least important conv5_3 units, leaving its 20 most important units.
rows.measure: Mean reduction in balanced single-class accuracy
rows.locator: Results, Role of Units in a Scene Classifier; Figure 2d
rows.check: Control row; same issue as r5.

rows.subject: Progressive GAN
rows.stage_stated: trained on LSUN outdoor church scenes
rows.operation_detail: Matched units in layer5 to segmented visual concepts using network dissection; reported concepts with IoU above 4%.
rows.measure: Number of units matching each concept type
rows.value: 19 object-specific units, 41 units matching object parts, one material unit, and six color units
rows.locator: Results, Emergence of Object Detectors in a GAN; Figure 3d
rows.note: These are counts of units by concept type, not shares of poles with one main job.
rows.check: Wrong training set and layer size. Figure 3 and the text describe the dissected GAN as trained on LSUN kitchens, not outdoor churches. The layer analysed is layer5 (16x16, 512 units), not layer4. The count of 67 concept-matched units out of 512 only counts units with IoU > 4%, so it is not a single-job share.

rows.subject: Progressive GAN
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated unit 314 as a classifier for whether generated images contain a large window, using peak activation.

conditions.value: 800 with windows larger than 5% of image area and 800 without

rows.measure: Accuracy predicting whether an image has a large window
rows.value: 78.2% using a threshold of peak activation > 8.03
rows.locator: Results, Emergence of Object Detectors in a GAN; Figure 3f-g
rows.note: The paper also notes that large windows can be generated without this unit activating.

rows.subject: Progressive GAN
rows.stage_stated: trained on LSUN outdoor church scenes
rows.operation_detail: Removed the 20 most tree-specific units in layer4, ranked by IoU with tree segmentations.
rows.uncertainty: 99% confidence intervals shown in Figure 4a; interval values not stated
rows.locator: Results, Role of Units in a GAN; Figure 4a-b
rows.note: The text says other objects such as buildings remained unchanged and generated images continued to look similarly realistic.

rows.subject: Progressive GAN
rows.stage_stated: trained on LSUN outdoor church scenes
rows.operation_detail: Forced the 20 most door-specific units in layer4 to their high threshold value at tested feature-map locations.

conditions.value: varied; examples include buildings, windows, trees, and sky

rows.measure: Whether door pixels were added to the generated scene
rows.value: Doors could be added in appropriate locations, such as buildings or windows; it was nearly impossible to add one on a tree or in the sky.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviation shown in Figure 4d; values not stated
rows.locator: Results, Role of Units in a GAN; Figure 4c-d
rows.note: The study reports that the same activation could produce different doors, or no door, depending on location and scene context.
